title: Compliance Reporting Pack (Baseline) — Outline Draft (WIP)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the working outline for the “Baseline Compliance Reporting Pack” deliverable.
- Audience: customer security reviewers (primary), customer auditors/internal controls team (secondary), Redwood internal audit readiness (secondary).
- This is NOT a SOC 2 report / ISO certificate. It is an evidence package + configuration export + coverage summary.

Status
- Draft outline + placeholders.
- Pending: confirmation of export formats, final naming, and which screenshots we will include in the customer-facing PDF vs console-export attachments.

Assumptions / Constraints
- Pack can be generated on-demand for a specific tenant + time window.
- Output format for v1: customer-facing PDF (or PDF-like rendered doc) + machine-readable attachments (JSON/CSV) + evidence checklist.
- We should avoid including sensitive operational internals (exact infrastructure hostnames, internal alert thresholds, etc.).
- Any “examples” must be explicitly labeled as examples; customer copies should reflect only their tenant.

Proposed package structure (baseline)

0. Cover Page
- Title: Redwood Inference — Compliance Reporting Pack (Baseline)
- Customer name / tenant id
- Report generated timestamp (UTC)
- Covered time window for audit logs (e.g., 2025-02-01 to 2025-03-01)
- Deployment mode: Hosted API | Dedicated | Private
- Region(s)/data residency setting(s)
- Pack version (e.g., baseline-v0.1)

Placeholder notes
- Need to finalize versioning scheme: baseline-v0.x vs report schema v1.0.
- Include “Confidential” footer? (GRC leaning yes; Product wants neutral language for smoother sharing.)

1. Executive Summary (1–2 pages)
- What this pack is and is not
- What the pack contains (bullet summary)
- How data retention settings are enforced at a high level
- Where to find additional artifacts: Security FAQ, DPA, pen test letter (if applicable), subprocessor list, etc. (links only)

Open question
- Do we include a “control mapping summary” in the executive summary or keep that as an appendix?

2. Scope & Definitions
2.1 Scope
- In scope (baseline): retention configuration export; audit log coverage summary; time-windowed audit log export; data residency/region summary; access control/RBAC report; evidence collection checklist.
- Out of scope (baseline): full custom reporting; bespoke GRC platform integration; per-field redaction policy proof; customer internal system evidence.

2.2 Definitions (short)
- “Request/response logs” vs “audit logs” (explicitly differentiate)
- “Retention policy” vs “logging configuration”
- “TTL” vs “purge” vs “hard delete”
- “Legal hold” (meaning + effect)

Draft definitions to align with Security FAQ
- Audit logs: immutable append-only record of administrative/security-relevant actions in Redwood control plane (e.g., login, API key changes, policy changes) + selected platform events.
- Request logs: operational logs of inference requests (may be disabled / redacted depending on configuration).

3. Tenant & Environment Summary
3.1 Tenant identifiers
- Tenant name
- Tenant ID / org ID
- Account tier: Hosted/Dedicated/Private

3.2 Deployment + region summary
- Control plane region
- Data plane region(s)
- Data residency configuration (if configured)
- Notes on cross-region processing/failover behavior (high level, no internal runbooks)

Placeholder
- Confirm whether we can safely include: “fallback enabled/disabled” statements in customer pack (Product prefers minimal; Security says may be asked).

4. Retention Controls Summary (Customer Configuration)
Goal
- Provide a clear, customer-readable description of what is retained, for how long, and what exceptions exist.

4.1 Retention policy overview
- Where retention settings are applied (control plane policy evaluation; enforcement by purge jobs per store)
- Change history is audited

4.2 Retention by data class (table)
Include rows for:
- Audit logs
- Request/response logs (if applicable / if enabled)
- Traces
- Metrics
- Artifacts (e.g., eval datasets / prompt sets) — only if supported for the customer’s deployment mode
For each row include columns:
- Data class
- Storage location type (high-level: “telemetry store”, “audit log store”) (avoid vendor naming unless approved)
- Configured retention duration (days)
- Effective retention (if differs due to tier constraints)
- Purge schedule (e.g., daily) — confirm if we should state “daily” vs “periodic”
- Deletion semantics (hard delete vs tombstone) — GRC wants clarity; Eng says we only guarantee deletion from primary stores, backups follow standard backup retention

4.3 Retention configuration export (attachment)
- Attachment: retention-config.json
- Include schema version
- Include last modified timestamp + actor

4.4 Legal hold and exceptions (short section)
- Whether legal hold is active for tenant (boolean)
- If active: high-level explanation of impact (retention extended / deletion paused for specified classes)
- Workflow summary: approvals required (CISO/legal) and audit trail

GRC comment (Olga)
- We need to be extremely careful with “legal hold is active” wording; for most customers it will be false. If it’s true, confirm what we are allowed to disclose.

Product comment (Naomi)
- Keep this section short. Most customers ask “can you do a legal hold,” not the details.

5. Audit Log Coverage Summary
Goal
- Demonstrate audit logging exists, what categories of events are captured, and how exports were produced.

5.1 Coverage statement
- List event categories included (examples): Authentication, Authorization/RBAC changes, API key lifecycle, Retention policy changes, Report pack generation events, Tenant configuration changes, Administrative access events (where applicable).

5.2 Known limitations (if any)
- E.g., “Some data-plane operational events may be in telemetry logs, not audit logs”
- If any event types are not available for this deployment mode, state explicitly.

5.3 Audit-log export details
- Export time window
- Filters applied
- Export format(s): CSV + JSON (confirm)
- Integrity notes: ordering, timestamps, unique IDs

Attachments
- audit-log-export.csv
- audit-log-export.json (optional, if we deliver both)

Engineering input needed (Kevin)
- Confirm what the exporter can include in v1: templates + time window + actor/event filters + bundling retention-config attachment.

6. Access Control / RBAC Report
Goal
- Provide a “who can do what” snapshot suitable for auditors.

6.1 RBAC model summary
- Roles available (platform-defined + any custom roles)
- Permission groups relevant to compliance: retention policy admin, audit log viewer/exporter, org admin, billing admin

6.2 Tenant role assignments (attachment)
- Users/service accounts
- Roles assigned
- MFA status (if available) (open question)
- Last login (open question)

6.3 Access control change history (optional)
- Either a short list of changes in the window or reference to audit log filter.

Product comment (Naomi)
- Keep “MFA status” and “last login” out unless we’re confident it’s accurate across SSO + SCIM, otherwise it becomes a support burden.

GRC comment (Olga)
- Auditors always ask for “privileged access list.” If we can’t do MFA/last login, we should at least provide the list of principals with privileged roles + timestamp of report generation.

7. Data Residency / Data Location Summary
Goal
- Help customer confirm where data is stored/processed, tied to configuration.

7.1 Configured residency
- “Pinned region” vs “multi-region” (use product terms)
- Any customer-selected constraints

7.2 Where data is stored (high-level)
- Audit logs store region
- Telemetry store region(s)
- Report pack artifact storage region (if applicable)

7.3 Notes on transient processing
- “Requests may be processed in-region; no cross-region processing unless configured for failover” (confirm exact statement)

Placeholder
- Need final copy from Security/Legal on what we can state without creating contractual commitments.

8. Retention Enforcement Verification (Optional for Customer Pack; recommended for Internal Pack)
Goal
- Provide evidence we enforce retention (purges happen; lag is monitored).

Option A (customer-facing)
- 1 paragraph describing monitoring exists + that purge jobs are idempotent + monitored.
- Include a single chart screenshot showing “TTL lag within SLO” for their tenant (if multi-tenant safe and if we can filter by tenant without exposing other tenants).

Option B (internal)
- Provide dashboard links + alert history summary.

SRE comment (Sean)
- Do not include raw dashboard screenshots that reveal cluster names or unrelated tenant data. If we can’t produce a tenant-scoped chart, omit.

9. Evidence Collection Checklist (Attachment + Appendix)
Goal
- Provide an auditor-friendly checklist and “what to ask Redwood for next.”

Checklist items
- Retention config export attached
- Audit log export attached (time window X)
- RBAC snapshot attached
- Data residency summary included
- Contact for questions (Security/GRC alias)

Add “Control mapping hints” (SOC2/ISO style)
- CC6.x (logical access), CC7.x (monitoring), CC8.x (change management), A.5/A.8/A.12 style references (keep generic)

GRC comment (Olga)
- Keep mappings as “informational” and not a claim of compliance.

10. Appendices
A. Report generation metadata
- Generated by (system)
- Generation job id
- Pack version
- Hash/checksum of attachments (open question; would be nice-to-have)

B. Export schemas
- Schema versions for retention-config.json, rbac-export.json, audit log export columns

C. Glossary
- Expand abbreviations: TTL, RBAC, SSO, SCIM, KMS (avoid going too deep)

D. Change log for the reporting pack (template)
- baseline-v0.1: initial release


Screenshots / visuals to add (placeholder list)
- Console: Retention Settings page (default view)
- Console: Retention change history drawer
- Console: “Download compliance pack” action (if implemented)
- Example table: retention by data class (customer-specific)
- Audit log export UI (if any) OR sample of exported fields (with redactions)
- RBAC “Users & roles” page (if exists)
- (Optional) Tenant-scoped retention verification chart (TTL lag) — only if sanitized

NOTE: All screenshots must be taken from a dedicated test tenant (no real customer identifiers) unless explicitly approved for that customer copy.


Review comments / open issues
1) Naming
- “Compliance Reporting Pack” vs “Evidence Pack” vs “Audit Evidence Pack”
- Product preference: “Compliance Reporting Pack (Baseline)” (less scary than “audit”).
- GRC preference: include the word “evidence” in subtitle to set expectations.

2) Legal hold semantics
- Need final wording approved by Sofia Mendes + Aisha Rahman.
- Ensure we don’t imply we can preserve everything indefinitely in all tiers without an exception process.

3) Default retention periods by tier
- Make sure we do not embed defaults in the pack unless they reflect the tenant’s configured policy (or the pack is explicitly “policy defaults” document).
- If customer is on Hosted with limited controls, we should show what they can configure vs fixed defaults.

4) Data plane vs control plane
- Avoid technical detail, but we should clearly say: policy changes are audited; enforcement is automated; purges are monitored.

5) Export format versioning
- Need alignment with ADR-018. Minimum: include “schema_version” field in JSON attachments and “pack_version” in the PDF.

6) Security review workload reduction
- Add a one-page “What to send to your auditor” section? (Naomi suggestion)
- GRC: okay if it’s an appendix.


Proposed next steps
- Naomi + Olga: finalize customer-facing section list (what goes in PDF vs attachments).
- Kevin: confirm attachment list and export fields supported in MVP.
- Daniel: draft evidence checklist wording + control mapping hints (informational only).
- Elliot: prepare “glossary + definitions” copy consistent with Security FAQ.

Questions to resolve (for next review)
- Do we include backup retention statements? If yes, where and how specific?
- Do we include “report pack generation is itself audited” (nice trust-building point) — confirm it’s implemented.
- Are we delivering RBAC as a screenshot only, or an export attachment?
- Can we support per-region summaries in multi-region tenants without extra engineering?

Rough timeline (not a commitment)
- Outline freeze: end of next week
- First end-to-end generation run (internal): within 2 weeks after exporter changes land
- Customer pilot pack: design partner request-driven
